Watch what happens when a basketball is dropped from a 415-foot dam At the Gordon Dam in Tasmania, which stands 415 feet high, a simple experiment with a basketball produced an unexpected result. When dropped normally, the ball falls almost straight down. But when released with backspin, the ball suddenly shoots sideways through the air. The surprising motion is caused by the Magnus effect, a force that affects spinning objects moving through air and plays a major role in sports like tennis, soccer, and golf. 2 charged during investigation into 9-year-old girl's death in Pennsylvania Two more people are facing charges in the death of 9-year-old Renesmay Eutsey.
